cues.en: In this chapter, we want to have a look at advanced batch features.
Those are topics that didn't made it into the other chapters here, and those are pretty advanced features.
Nonetheless, it's great if you know about them and you know that they exist.
The features or the things that we will have a look at here would be, for example, how we can change
a directory without needing the CD command for this, how we can have batch correct errors for us.
We will have a quick look at extended globbing that allows us to further define how files should be
found.
We will have a look at how we can turn on errors when Globbing didn't succeed instead of just having
them silently being ignored.
Meaning if we were to try to using or if we would try to use a file name expansion and it wouldn't find
any files, that we would get an actual error there and not just the original value.
And we will also have a look at how we can work with the bash history.
Those are all useful things and they didn't really made it into the other chapters because when we looked
at Globbing first, for example, it was enough to understand the normal globbing for now.
But now that we have already looked for so many hours into Bash Linux and then Shell scripting again,
now we can also talk about advanced features that are not that common, but they are still useful quite
often.
And this is what this chapter here is for.
So in the next lecture, we want to have a look at how we can enable that.
We can change the directory without needing the CD command.
